title: Cerebellar Brain Stimulation Plus Language Therapy for People at Risk of Poor Aphasia Recovery After Stroke
official: Predicting Aphasia Recovery and Testing Cerebellar Neuromodulation (PART-CN): A Pilot Wait-List Randomized Trial of Cathodal Cerebellar Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Plus Computerized Language Therapy in Stroke Survivors Predicted to Have Poor Language Recovery
summary:
This pilot study tests whether a mild form of brain stimulation to the cerebellum, combined with computer-based language therapy, helps people recover language after a stroke when a poor natural recovery is predicted.

People already taking part in a Johns Hopkins study of stroke and language recovery, whose early data suggest the aphasia is unlikely to resolve without treatment, are invited about 3 months after the stroke. Half begin 15 treatment sessions right away and half begin about 3 months later. Each session pairs 25 minutes of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the right cerebellum with 45 to 60 minutes of language exercises, with a speech-language pathologist present.

The main question is whether language ability, measured with the Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Aphasia Quotient, improves more by 6 months after stroke in the group treated first than in the group still waiting. The study also checks how accurately a machine learning model, built from data collected in the first days after stroke, predicted each person's language ability 12 months after stroke.

interventions.name: Cathodal cerebellar transcranial direct current stimulation

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Enrolled in the Johns Hopkins longitudinal stroke and aphasia study (IRB NA\_00042097)
* Consented to future contact for research studies
* Predicted to have poor language recovery from acute-phase data, defined as a predicted Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Aphasia Quotient below 93.8 at 12 months post-stroke
* Ischemic left hemisphere stroke
* Aphasia with naming impairment on the Western Aphasia Battery-Revised
* Approaching 3 months post-stroke at enrollment
* Fluent speaker of English by self-report
* Age 18 or older

Exclusion Criteria:

* Lesion in the right cerebellum
* Previous neurological disorder other than stroke affecting the brain, or any neurodegenerative or psychiatric disorder
* Seizures during the previous 6 months
* Uncorrected visual or hearing loss by self-report
* Use of medications that lower the seizure threshold (e.g., methylphenidate)
* Use of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists (e.g., memantine)
* History of brain surgery or any metal in the head
* Severely impaired auditory comprehension (below 2 on the Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Auditory Verbal Comprehension sub-score)
* Severely limited verbal output (below 2 on the Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Spontaneous Speech rating)
